newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FOCUS-output, gold price hits JCI Q1 profit.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-output, gold price hits JCI Q1 profit.

text.p: JCI Ltd reported sharply reduced pre-capex net earnings for the March quarter on Tuesday as a lower rand gold price and lower output from two of the South African mining house's three mines slashed profits.
JCI's gold mines posted a 67 percent drop in profit to 44.24 million rand from the 132.89 million in the three months to end-December.
Gold production was down 8.9 percent at 10,676 kg from the 11,724 kg in the previous quarter.
"All in all, it was a difficult quarter for the mines," JCI gold and uranium division chief executive John Brownrigg said at a results presentation.
HJ Joel was the best performer, lifting pre-capex net profit slightly to 40,205 million rand from the 40,099 million in the previous quarter.
But Western Areas Gold Mining Company Ltd saw profits reduced by 85.9 percent to 6.9 million rand from 48.97 million in the three months to December.
And Randfontein Estates Gold Mining Co continued the losses by reporting a loss of 2.86 million rand from a profit of 43.83 million rand in the December quarter.
"Significant decreases at both Randfontein Estates and Western Areas resulted in adverse variances in respect of tonnage milled, yield and kilograms produced," Brownrigg said.
Throughput at Randfontein dropped to 1,684,000 tonnes from 1,732,000 and at Western Areas from 737,000 tonnes in the December quarter to 691,000 in the three months to end-March.
"We were shocked at the (Randfontein) results," Brownrigg said.
The three mines also suffered from a lower rand gold price received and JCI said it received 52,819 rand for every kg of gold produced -- down 5.8 percent on the previous quarter.
"We are now receiving a rand gold price lower than one year ago," Brownrigg said.
But he said in order to address the major problems faced by the mines, management, unions and JCI's new owners recently agreed to develop a "Strategic Labour Accord".
"The objective of the accord is to implement changes at all three mines that will improve and sustain operational productivity for the benefit of all stakeholders.
Black empowerment consortium African Mining Group won a bid to buy Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd's 34.9 percent stake in JCI last year.
The deal gives black business a significant interest in the South African mining industry for the first time.
